## Example 1.5 {#gac2-example-1-5 .gac-lesson}

Find the first, second, third and fourth derivatives for

$$y=7x^3+4x^2-2x+1$$

<p class="booklet-cue">Example 1.5 · Booklet p. 9</p>

::: notes
6 minutes. Preserve the booklet question; complete the working in OneNote.

First derivative: y'=21x^2+8x-2.

Second derivative: y''=42x+8.

Third derivative: y'''=42.

Fourth derivative: y^{(4)}=0.

Before calculating the fourth derivative, ask students to predict it and justify their prediction. Zero is a valid derivative, not an undefined derivative. Every later derivative is also zero. Emphasise differentiating the result of the previous step rather than repeatedly restarting with the original expression.
:::
